newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-SPINNERS FIGHT BACK, BUT AUSTRALIA STILL ON TOP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SPINNERS FIGHT BACK, BUT AUSTRALIA STILL ON TOP.

text.p: West Indies spinners Carl Hooper and Shivnarine Chanderpaul hit back in the session before tea, taking three wickets to rein in Australia's attempt to build a huge lead on the second day of their fourth test match.
Australia went to tea at 330 for five on Sunday after extending their lead over the West Indies' paltry first innings total of 130.
But the runs came at the cost of maiden test century-maker Matthew Hayden for 125 and an ominously in-form Mark Waugh for 82.
Right arm off spinner Carl Hooper was the pick of the West Indies bowlers, taking the wickets of Hayden and Waugh for 25 runs in a 10 over spell of tight, flat bowling that included two maidens.
Frustrated by a slowdown in the scoring rate on a gentle wicket, Hayden bounded down the pitch to a Hooper delivery just short of a length and was stumped in a trice by Junior Murray.
The wicketkeeper's victory must have seemed bittersweet, however, as he had dived across in front of Brian Lara at first slip and dropped Hayden when he was on 82 before lunch.
Murray had also allowed a catch from Hayden to fly between himself and Lara late on Saturday when Hayden was on 58.

Words and glares were exchanged again in the slips this morning after the mix-up. Captain and bowler Courtney Walsh appeared inconsolable, his eyes to the heavens and his arms outstretched in disbelief.
Right arm legspinner Chanderpaul was also an effective foil to the West Indies' pace-dominated attack, if somewhat unconventional.
He snared the prize wicket of Steve Waugh for 26 with a rank long hop that was punched into the covers, only to be scooped up by a sprawling Carl Hooper.
Despite the setback, Australia have a stranglehold on the match and look set to post a large total and ensure a draw at least, which would be enough for them to retain the Frank Worrell trophy.
Australia lead the best of five match series 2-1.
Earlier the left-handed Hayden scored his maiden test century in his third test match for Australia.

The 25-year-old Queenslander struggled early the session, freezing on his overnight score of 66 for an agonising 43 minutes, a period that included being caught out slashing a wide ball to cover off a no ball from Bishop.
But as his confidence returned, Hayden plundered some wayward fast bowling from Cameron Cuffy and Patterson Thompson and raced to his century.
Hayden cut decisively backwards of point off Cuffy to bring up the ton in 267 minutes from 179 balls with 14 fours.

Hayden, who struggled for test selection for the last five years despite hefty scores in the domestic arena, crossed himself and raised his bat in salute to a standing ovation from the crowd of over 20,000 and the dressing room.
